name: DWP Universal Credit Health statistics — the LCWRA (health element) caseload by entitlement rate, April to June 2026

model.name: DWP administrative data (Stat-Xplore, UC - Work Capability Assessments)
model.method: Claimants on UC health at the second Thursday of each month, by the LCWRA entitlement rate (Note 6). The count is the rate a claimant is entitled to, not the amount paid that month (Note 7). Great Britain.

scope_note: First tranche of #87: Table 2 (LCWRA caseload by entitlement rate, April to June 2026) and the lower rate's share of the June total. The child, housing, carer and childcare element counts are on Stat-Xplore, which needs an account; they stay open on #87.
boundary_note: The counts are administrative outturns, which the 2026-08-02 boundary rule sends to the Chronicle ledger. They are staged as claims (2026-10-23), following the Census STC (#176) and ONS CPI (lane uk-benefit-uprating) decisions: the health element's rates are what an Autumn Budget 2026 freeze or cut acts on, and the new-claimant share has a direct PolicyEngine-UK counterpart.
calibration_evidence: Held out. The certified bundle populace-uk-2023-dd68c73-4aa4b14-20260619T023711Z calibrates to 149 targets: 142 ONS, 6 SLC and 1 OBR, and no DWP target (calibration_diagnostics.json in PolicyEngine/microcosm@7f235941 packages/microcosm-data/tests/fixtures/uk_june_2023/, read 2026-10-22). policyengine-uk-data main targets/sources/dwp.py (read 2026-10-22) targets UC by number of children and family type, and no LCWRA count. The dd68c73 commit is not on GitHub, so its own dwp.py could not be read.
diagnosis_upstream: A gap in the new-claimant share is a policyengine-uk parameter question (gov.dwp.universal_credit.rebalancing.new_claimant_share).
